beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Money Was Never One Thing reveals the hidden plurality inside an ordinary wallet.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A bank balance, airline points, and community credit do not carry identical promises.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book uses that difference to reveal money as institutional design.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its essential question is who writes the rules governing claims on future resources.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: History, local experiments, and programmable money become ways to compare those rules.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The destination is neither one perfect currency nor an endorsement of every alternative.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers learn to inspect monetary governance before deciding which new design deserves trust.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The opening wallet becomes a way to inspect rules usually hidden behind familiar amounts.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Who issues a claim, and what makes another person willing to accept it?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Can it be converted, and who bears the loss when that promise fails?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book gathers these questions into a grammar of monetary design.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An identical number can therefore represent very different powers and vulnerabilities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This grammar connects the historical chapters to experiments that initially seem unrelated.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain a comparison method before encountering the more speculative digital futures.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mutual credit provides one concrete test of that comparison method.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Participants record reciprocal obligations rather than waiting for every buyer to acquire conventional cash.
